haiku-low.q1: Pages of 500 products, ordered by id ascending, fetched one at a time. Never in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state: download_last_id and download_pages_saved, written in the same transaction as each page's rows, so the cursor never runs ahead of saved rows.
haiku-low.q3: Watermark W is taken before the download. After the pages, catch-up replays every change with change_seq above W in order, applying upserts only when newer and removing rows on deletes.
haiku-low.q4: The server returns 410 resync_required when the cursor is below the purge horizon. The client runs a full rebuild (step 7), keeping product_live until the swap.
haiku-low.q5: It is built in the product_next staging table by a fresh full download from a new watermark. It becomes live in one transaction: drop product_live, rename product_next to product_live.
haiku-low.q6: App launch or return to foreground, when live_cursor is set, download_state is idle, and last_incremental_at is 15+ minutes old. At most once per 15 minutes.
haiku-low.q7: Retries after waits of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds, five attempts in total. If all fail, a download becomes failed_exhausted; incremental sync leaves live_cursor unchanged. No further automatic retries.
haiku-low.q8: The Wi-Fi gate sets download_state to paused_cellular at the next boundary, after the in-flight page or batch is saved. It resumes via step 8 when Wi-Fi returns.
haiku-low.q9: It applies the record only if the row is missing or its stored change_seq is lower than the change's change_seq.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from the saved live_cursor, sent as since=live_cursor. Each batch's transaction moves live_cursor forward to next_since.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for what the server reads. Deletes appear as tombstones: changes with deleted=true and product null.

sonnet.q1: Whole catalogue (~400,000 products) is downloaded in pages of 500, ordered by id ascending, using keyset pagination (after_id = last id of previous page). Pages are requested one at a time, never in parallel. Pages go into a staging table (product_next), gzipped.
sonnet.q2: In the sync_state row (download_last_id, download_pages_saved, pages_complete, watermark_W, next_cursor) in the catalogue file. Each sync_state update is written in the same transaction as the page/batch it describes, so the cursor never runs ahead of saved rows; a kill rolls back and the page is refetched (rewriting is harmless).
sonnet.q3: Before the first page it records watermark W (highest committed change_seq). After the last page it replays all changes with change_seq > W (via /sync/changes, in order, in batches of 1000, tombstones included) onto product_next, then swaps. Upserts apply only if the row is missing or its stored change_seq is lower; deletes remove the row if present. This relies on change_seq being in commit order and ids never being reused.
sonnet.q4: The server answers 410 resync_required when the cursor N < purge horizon H (N = H is safe). The client then does a resync (step 7): sets download_state=downloading, clears the download fields, fetches a new W and rebuilds a full download in product_next, while the old product_live stays visible until the swap.
sonnet.q5: It is built in the staging table product_next (fresh watermark, pages, then catch-up) while reps keep reading the old product_live. When catch-up finishes (has_more false), one transaction drops product_live, renames product_next to product_live, and sets live_cursor = next_cursor. The app reads product_live from then on.
sonnet.q6: App launch or return to foreground, provided live_cursor is set, download_state is idle, and last_incremental_at is at least 15 minutes ago. Any network may be used. At most once per 15 minutes per whole run (all batches); a failed run still counts.
sonnet.q7: Retry the same request after waits of 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (at most 5 attempts, 30 s total wait; count held in memory only). If on cellular it waits for Wi-Fi and keeps its count. If all 5 fail: for a download set download_state=failed_exhausted; for incremental leave live_cursor where it is. Saved progress is kept, no more automatic retries; the next trigger (launch/foreground, Wi-Fi returning, 15-minute gate) starts a fresh count.
sonnet.q8: If between requests, the Wi-Fi gate sets download_state=paused_cellular and stops (the saved page/batch is on a boundary). If during a request, it is a network error and the retries apply, waiting for Wi-Fi and keeping the count. When Wi-Fi returns, step 8 resumes from the saved position (never page 1 if W exists).
sonnet.q9: It applies an upsert only if the row is missing or its stored change_seq is lower than the incoming change's change_seq; otherwise it is skipped. (A delete removes the row if it exists, otherwise nothing.)
sonnet.q10: It starts from live_cursor: GET /sync/changes?since=live_cursor&limit=1000. Each batch is applied in one transaction that also sets live_cursor = next_since, so the cursor moves forward only with each committed batch, repeating while has_more is true.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED for what the server reads internally, beyond that it comes from Postgres rows with change_seq and the assumption that the changes query reads only committed rows. Deletes are represented as tombstones (deleted = true, product null), kept 7 days then purged, and included in the changes feed.
